players.product: Revio and Vega HiFi long-read sequencing platforms

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mark Van Oene: on June 13 the New England Journal of Medicine published 'Clinical Long-Read Genome Sequencing for Rare Disease Diagnostics' (Bitter et al.): concordance between long-read genome sequencing and standard of care was 96.4%; long-read improved or refined diagnoses in 3.4% of cases, while standard of care only caught variants that long-reads missed in 0.2% of cases. Management says the publication demonstrates that HiFi long-read sequencing is a clinically effective first-tier diagnostic test and believes it carries real weight with payers and health systems. A Nature Genetics article (Sabbagh et al.) proposed long-read genome sequencing as one pillar of 'near-perfect genome sequencing', and a preprint from the HiFi Solves subfertility consortium in Asia Pacific (its first major study) showed HiFi genome sequencing can provide a complete view of reproductive genetics in a single workflow.
quarterly_data.figure: concordance 96.4%; diagnoses improved or refined in 3.4% of cases; standard of care caught variants long-reads missed in 0.2% of cases

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 EMEA revenue of $14.4 million increased 52%, reflecting continued clinical adoption as hospitals and clinical customers transitioned from pilot programs into routine production, growing Vega demand and a significant strategic multi-system Revio placement supporting a large-scale national genomics initiative; Americas revenue of $17.6 million was down slightly on NIH and broader academic funding uncertainty; Asia Pacific revenue of $7 million decreased 45%, primarily on the conclusion of a significant population sequencing program, academic and government funding headwinds and lower consumables demand during SPRQ-Nx workflow validation. CEO: clinical shipments were a mid-teens percentage of total consumable shipments, the majority of Q2 Revio placements went to clinical accounts, specific clinical customers are exiting R&D mode into routine production sequencing, U.S. public health labs purchased Vega instruments, with momentum starting in wastewater testing, and 81% of Vega shipments went to new customers; EMEA is expected to remain the fastest-growing region in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: EMEA $14.4 million (+52%); Americas $17.6 million; Asia Pacific $7 million (-45%); clinical mid-teens % of consumable shipments; 81% of Vega shipments to new customers

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: 2026 non-GAAP gross margin is now expected at 35% to 37% (reflecting approximately $2.5 million of temporary Vega manufacturing transition costs, elevated compute and memory costs, a more gradual SPRQ-Nx adoption curve and lower-priced strategic Revio placements) and non-GAAP operating expenses at $215 million to $220 million, a reduction of $5 million from the range guided in Q1. CEO: full-year consumables pull-through is now expected at $200,000 to $225,000 per Revio system, a range management anticipates increasing as the SPRQ-Nx transition rolls into late 2026 and 2027. CFO: cash flow breakeven is now expected in 2028 versus the prior expectation of the end of 2027; the restructuring is expected to reduce compensation-related expenses by approximately $15 million to $20 million next year, with approximately $15 million to $20 million of additional annual savings as the company moves past development spending on its high-throughput platform.
quarterly_data.figure: non-GAAP gross margin 35% to 37%; non-GAAP opex $215 million to $220 million; pull-through $200,000 to $225,000 per Revio system; cash flow breakeven 2028 (prior: end of 2027)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 gross margin absorbed $1.1 million of costs from transitioning Vega manufacturing in-house from its contract manufacturer; these transition costs are expected to conclude by the end of 2026, and the insourcing is aimed at cutting long-term costs and reducing the number of suppliers. Cash outflows were higher on strategic purchases of memory components; based on its current forecast PacBio has memory and GPU coverage through the end of 2026, will probably start purchasing more memory at the tail end of this year, and does not yet have good visibility into 2027. The CFO does not expect memory costs to necessarily decrease but sees early indicators that spot-market fluctuations are starting to stabilize.
quarterly_data.figure: Vega manufacturing transition costs $1.1 million (Q2); memory and GPU supply covered through end of 2026
